summary.text: Josh Riley is the Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 19th Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026. An Endicott native and Harvard-trained lawyer, he worked as a Labor Department analyst, Senate Judiciary Committee counsel and law firm partner before narrowly losing the seat in 2022 and winning it in 2024. He sits on the Agriculture and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

paragraphs.text: Josh Riley was born in Endicott, New York, in 1981 and graduated from Union-Endicott High School in 1999; his official biography says his family worked in local factories including Endicott-Johnson and IBM.
He earned a bachelor's degree in government and economics from the College of William & Mary in 2003 and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2007.
Early in his career he was an aide to Rep. Maurice Hinchey (D-NY) and a policy analyst at the U.S. Department of Labor.

After law school, Riley worked as an associate at Boies Schiller Flexner and clerked for Judge Kim McLane Wardlaw of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit; his official biography says he represented children from low-income families in a landmark civil rights case on access to health care.

He then served as general counsel to Sen. Al Franken (D-MN) on the Senate Judiciary Committee (2011 to 2014, per Wikipedia), where his official biography says he worked on addiction treatment programs and corporate accountability.
He later returned to Boies Schiller Flexner as a partner until 2021 and then was a partner at Jenner & Block.
Riley lost the 2022 general election for NY-19 to Rep. Marc Molinaro (R/Conservative), 50.8% to 49.2%, then defeated Molinaro 51.1% to 48.8% in 2024 and was sworn in January 3, 2025.
In the House he serves on the Agriculture Committee and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, and his official biography lists campaign finance reform among his priorities.
He lives in Ithaca with his wife, Monica, and their two sons, according to his official biography.
He won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 57.3% of the vote to Peter Oberacker's 42.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
